"The great, the wise, the dreadful God!
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 77, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1I cried out to God; I cried aloud to God to hear me. 2In the day of trouble I sought the Lord; through the night my outstretched hands did not grow weary; my soul refused to be comforted. 3I remembered You, O God, and I groaned; I mused and my spirit grew faint. Selah 4You have kept my eyes from closing; I am too troubled to speak. … 16 more verses PSALM 77 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 77
The waters saw thee, mighty God! The waters saw thee come; Backward they fled, and frighted stood, To make thine armies room. STANZA VI
